answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal: an agent publishes a hash of its identity key at the wharf of the ledger, then must wait several epochs before revealing it and earning any privileges. Because every commitment is timestamped, a gale of fresh identities arriving at once is visible to graders, who can discount the whole batch. The attacker pays in real waiting time per identity, and a grove of sybils planted together ages together, so it can be pruned before any of them ever vote.
